subChunks.title: Modals and Dialogs
subChunks.hookHtml: Modals are high-stakes UI components. They demand full-screen overlays, keyboard focus trapping, scroll locking, and proper ARIA markup — all to create the impression of a focused interruption. The Tailwind classes for modals are simple; the challenge is understanding how they work together.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
The modal overlay pattern

/* Overlay — covers the entire viewport, dims everything behind */
<div class="fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-black/50
            flex items-center justify-center
            p-4"  <!-- padding prevents modal touching screen edge on mobile -->
     role="dialog" aria-modal="true">

  /* Modal panel */
  <div class="bg-white rounded-xl shadow-xl
              w-full max-w-md
              max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto">
    <!-- modal content -->
  </div>
</div>

Modal anatomy

/* Header */
<div class="flex items-center justify-between p-6 border-b border-gray-100">
  <h2 class="text-lg font-semibold text-gray-900" id="modal-title">Confirm Action</h2>
  <button class="text-gray-400 hover:text-gray-600 transition-colors"
          aria-label="Close dialog">
    ×
  </button>
</div>

/* Body */
<div class="p-6">
  <p class="text-sm text-gray-600">This action cannot be undone.</p>
</div>

/* Footer */
<div class="flex items-center justify-end gap-3 p-6 border-t border-gray-100">
  <button class="px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 hover:bg-gray-100 rounded-md">
    Cancel
  </button>
  <button class="px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium bg-red-600 hover:bg-red-700 text-white rounded-md">
    Confirm Delete
  </button>
</div>

Animated modal entrance

/* Overlay — fade in */
<div class="fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-black/50
            flex items-center justify-center p-4
            animate-in fade-in duration-200">  <!-- Tailwind v4 animate utilities -->

/* Panel — slide up */
<div class="... animate-in slide-in-from-bottom-4 duration-200">

Or using standard utilities with transition classes from JavaScript state:

/* Overlay: opacity transition */
{isOpen ? 'opacity-100' : 'opacity-0 pointer-events-none'}
transition-opacity duration-200

/* Panel: translate transition */
{isOpen ? 'translate-y-0 opacity-100' : 'translate-y-4 opacity-0'}
transition duration-200

Sizes

max-w-sm    /* compact confirmation dialog */
max-w-md    /* standard dialog */
max-w-lg    /* form modal */
max-w-2xl   /* content-rich modal */
max-w-screen-md  /* nearly full screen */

Accessibility requirements

  • role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" on the modal container
  • aria-labelledby pointing to the modal title's id
  • Close button with aria-label="Close dialog"
  • Focus must be trapped inside the modal (requires JavaScript)
  • Pressing Escape must close the modal (requires JavaScript)
  • Scroll on body must be locked when modal is open (requires JavaScript)

Master Ember: "The overlay must be fixed inset-0 — not absolute. Fixed positions relative to the viewport so it covers the entire screen even when the page is scrolled. inset-0 is shorthand for top-0 right-0 bottom-0 left-0. Together they create a full-viewport cover. Then z-50 ensures it sits above all other content."

storyBeats.speaker: Master Ember
storyBeats.text: A modal demands the user's full attention — it must interrupt everything. fixed inset-0 covers the entire viewport. bg-black/50 dims what's behind. The panel inside must have a maximum height and overflow-y-auto so it never exceeds the screen, no matter how much content it holds.

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a form modal from scratch (no starter code): a modal overlay with backdrop, a panel containing a header (title + close button), a form body with two inputs (name and description), and a footer with cancel and save buttons. Add all accessibility attributes. Make the panel max-h-[90vh] with overflow-y-auto so long forms scroll inside the modal.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain why the modal overlay uses fixed inset-0 rather than absolute inset-0. Walk through each class on the overlay (fixed, inset-0, z-50, bg-black/50, flex items-center justify-center) and explain what removing any single one of them would break. Why does the panel need max-h-[90vh] and overflow-y-auto?

questions.prompt: A modal overlay uses absolute inset-0 instead of fixed inset-0. When the user scrolls down the page and opens the modal, the overlay doesn't cover the full visible screen. What is the cause?
options: absolute positions relative to the nearest positioned ancestor — if the body is scrolled, the overlay starts at the body top, not the viewport top. fixed always positions relative to the viewport
absolute needs a z-index to cover the viewport when scrolled
inset-0 only works with fixed positioning — it must be changed to top-0 right-0 bottom-0 left-0 for absolute
The body needs overflow-hidden for absolute overlays to work correctly
questions.answer: absolute positions relative to the nearest positioned ancestor — if the body is scrolled, the overlay starts at the body top, not the viewport top. fixed always positions relative to the viewport
questions.explanation: absolute positioning is relative to the nearest positioned ancestor (often the document root). When the user scrolls, absolute elements scroll with the page. fixed positioning is always relative to the viewport — it stays in place regardless of scroll position. Modal overlays must use fixed to cover the visible screen at any scroll position.

questions.prompt: A modal panel contains a long form that extends beyond the viewport height. Instead of cutting off, the panel should scroll internally while the overlay stays fixed. Which classes on the panel achieve this?
options: max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto — limits panel height to 90% of viewport and enables internal scrolling
h-screen overflow-scroll — sets full viewport height with scroll
max-height-screen overflow-hidden — restricts height and hides overflow
questions.answer: max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto — limits panel height to 90% of viewport and enables internal scrolling
questions.explanation: max-h-[90vh] prevents the panel from growing beyond 90% of the viewport height (leaving some gap at top/bottom). overflow-y-auto adds a scrollbar only when content exceeds this height. Together, they create a panel that scrolls internally when content is long, rather than overflowing the viewport.

questions.prompt: A modal is visually correct but screen reader users can still interact with elements behind it (the page content under the overlay). Which combination of attributes on the modal container addresses this?
options: role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" — aria-modal tells assistive technology to treat the content behind as inert
tabindex="-1" on all elements behind the modal
focus-trap class on the modal panel
questions.answer: role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" — aria-modal tells assistive technology to treat the content behind as inert
questions.explanation: role='dialog' announces the element as a dialog to screen readers. aria-modal='true' tells modern screen readers to restrict their virtual cursor to the dialog's content, treating everything behind it as inert. Without aria-modal, screen reader users can navigate to elements behind the overlay. Note: some older screen readers still require JavaScript focus trapping in addition to aria-modal.
